name: Theme color for browser UI
plain: Tints the browser's address bar or tab strip with a color the page picks.
meaning: A site can suggest a colour for the browser toolbar to match its brand. The tag is write only: it reveals nothing about the person, and the browser may ignore it.

access.persistence: Per page; the browser re-reads it on navigation or when the tag changes
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Only the top-level page's tag is used; iframes cannot set it
steps: Page includes a theme-color meta tag
Browser tints its toolbar on supported platforms

safari.note: From Safari 26, installed web apps only

limits.headline: Can tint your browser's address bar or tab strip with a color it picks
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Set the color of the address bar or tab strip
Pick a different color for dark mode
cannot: Change the browser's buttons, menus or other parts
Set a color in Firefox, which ignores it
limits.differs: Firefox ignores it. Chrome on computers only shows it in some window styles.

story.what_it_is: A page picks a color to tint your browser's address bar or tab strip.

marketing.name: theme-color meta tag
marketing.pitch: Documents the tag a page uses to suggest a color for the browser toolbar.

story.for_you: You see your browser bar change to match the site, such as green for a banking site or black for dark mode. It looks like part of the page.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for brand feel and to make web apps look native. It can also swap with dark mode. It is harmless, though a fake color can add to the look of a copycat site.

use_cases.example: A social site tints your phone address bar blue so it looks like its own app.
A browser game turns the browser bar black to blend with its dark menu.
A store paints the bar in its brand color on every product page.
A music site uses the album art color for the bar while a track plays.
A note app changes its bar color when you switch to dark mode.
A copycat bank page paints the bar the same color as the real bank to feel trusted.
A news site uses a red bar during live coverage.

technical_bounds: Chrome for Android (92) and Samsung Internet (6.2) tint the toolbar; Chrome Android skips it on devices with native dark mode unless the page is an installed app
Desktop Chrome (73) uses it only for installed PWA title bars
Safari 15 used it for the tab bar; from Safari 26 only installed web apps use it
Firefox desktop and Firefox for Android do not support it
A media attribute lets pages offer different colours for light and dark
The browser may ignore the colour for contrast or privacy

abuse: Mimicking system chrome colours to look trustworthy

history.change: Safari 15 uses theme-color for the tab bar on macOS and iOS
Chrome for Android actually applies the colour
Desktop Chrome applies it only to installed PWAs
